review_text:
Arabian Nights...with 5G Internet!
This was a fabulous stay. Perhaps the best stay of all my time Airb'nB.
It had been a while since I had last visited Mombasa, and I only had a few days, after a business event in Nairobi; so I wanted my stay to be efficient, calm and memorable.
Mohamed was a wonderful and caring host, who pretty much anticipated my every need. 
The apartment, on the top floor of a traditional Swahili family house, was wonderful: beautifully decorated and furnished in Omani-Mombasa style; featuring a magnificent four-poster bed, arabesque chill zone, clean bathroom and little kitchenette.
The let is above a well-known backpackers hostel in Mombasa Old Town, with a decent cafe on the ground-floor, within close walking distance of historic Fort Jesus (well-worth a visit) and a decent selection of stores selling tourist tat of varying quality.
But Mohamed and his cohort of fellow-fishermen are a welcoming and class act.
And this was--undoubtedly--a class stay.
Kurudi!

Got to kayak for about $5 per person, ride camels same rate, jetski for KSh2800/$28 per person for 10 minutes. From here you can take a cab to mtwapa for shopping it's just nearby about 15 minutes drive, or take a bike for KSh200.

The windows and balcony screens makes the whole apartment bug free and the place was spotty clean.  We were able to enjoy a little of everything from jet ski at East Coast watersports which is less that 7 minutes from the apartment, long beach walks from shanzu beach, bamburi beach to nyali beach right from the apartment beach front, and even a little golf at nyali golf club about 30 minutes drive for our golf lovers.  The pool is clean and accessible from 7am to 6pm.  My only surprise was that depending on what time you check the ocean the beach may disappear right in front of your eyes so you may walk out and plan to uber or tuk tuk back to the apartment if considering long walks.
We will sure come back for a longer stay...

However first night we encountered several issues:
We got to the house quite late in the big room, quite tired. There was Not a single drop of drinking water left for us in the house. Also not even one teabag or spoonful of coffee. While this is not a requirement for Airbnb, it would be a nice gesture to leave some of this stuff even just for the first night for guests who arrive too late to get out and shop for groceries. You can even include these in your room charges.
Shower: the most disappointing thing was that the shower was not working. We called the host and she was quite willing to assist and sent a plumber to fix it at around 11pm. While there was a slight improvement the water still only trickled from the shower. Mombasa is a hot and humid place and a good working shower with sufficient pressure is a MUST, hence our utter disappointment 
Bedroom
Quite spacious. However no dressing table/mirror in the room, no mosquito net either. We had uncomfortable nights that we had to deal with mosquitoes in the room and with no mosquito net or other mechanisms in place to get rid of mosquitoes, this made for quite an unpleasant experience 
Kitchen 
Had basic amenities. Nice patio facing the ocean where one could sit and relax. However some stools there would be great to place drinks while relaxing. Also we had another unpleasant experience where we tried to microwave a cup of tea and got scalded while taking out the cup. Please invest in quality microwave safe cups. 
Location
Nice location easy to get Ubers to different locations. Close to the ocean though the beach is really nothing to write home about as you really can’t walk on it- too rocky 
Best part
The house help is awesome. Polite, helpful, always at hand

The local bars and restaurants cater to a younger crowd, so if you’re an older couple like us, you’ll have to get a tuk tuk over the bridge to mellower places… unless we just missed some closer by
All in all, a great place to work from and experience the more bustling parts of Mombasa. Good for tourists, too, unless you need to be walking distance to the beach.

review_text:
My stay in the village of Kwa Ngombe - Naivasha was just what the doctor ordered - Peaceful. As a woman solo traveler, I appreciated that the on-site caretaker was non-problematic and helpful. I felt safe. I was able to walk deeper into the village and garner inspiration for my art. The serene garden gave me space to use my watercolors uninterrupted. The super hot water in the shower was soothing after a long day exploring. 
This Airbnb stay is walking distance to Sanctuary Farm - where you can walk amongst wild animals. The food at the farm is divine. The caretaker can arrange a boda rider to transport you in and around Naivasha, including to the KenGen Geo Thermal Spa. Enashipai Resort & Spa is a short boda ride away. Avian Court Hotel makes a wonderful breakfast. 
Unless you plan on dining out daily, I'd recommend packing groceries as there is no supermarket or online takeout service in the neighborhood. 
If you like simple, quiet, and safe lodging, you'll love this stay.

review_text:
A  restful, forested place to bring the our dogs for a weekend away from the city, but sadly our experience was let down by a few flaws in the listing and overall lack of communication by the host.
Most importantly, the host should be upfront that this is *BYO drinking water.* The tap water was dirty, murky, and had dead insects in it. The only mention of drinking water was buried at the bottom of the intro text from the host after we confirmed the booking. Since we didn't bring water, the property caretaker was forced to pay out of pocket for single-use plastic bottles of water to sustain us during our stay. At the price we paid,  drinking water should have been included, but at the very least this should have been mentioned in the Airbnb listing.
The map location tied to the listing is inaccurate, so we went down the wrong road for a few kms. The host did not respond to my message asking whether the pin was accurate, so our check-in experience was not as smooth as it could have been.
There was a big crack in the main living room window that made me worried to have my wife and dogs nearby. I did not want to test the integrity of the window but it looked like any small force could bring large glass shards crashing down. Does not seem safe to continue having guests with this issue, and it made the view a bit unsightly.
Couches and chairs in the living room are completely sunken in, providing little support or cushioning. There was no outdoor seating despite the presence of a pleasant front lawn. A menu of frozen foods was provided, but when we requested something from the caretaker, she was unable to access the freezer in the main house to get the food, so we were out of luck.
Overall the location was a relaxing place to bring the dogs for a short stay from Nairobi, but less relaxing than desired due to the issues outlined above. I would have been willing to overlook these flaws for a lower price and better communication.

review_text:
My trip to Kenya was for 5 weeks. Because of that I wanted someplace fantastic to stay. The catch was that I'd never been to Kenya before, so was quite honestly clueless about the accomodations there. But I read the reviews for the Nook@Hyrax and placed my trust in my fellow humans. 
I was not let down. 
During my 5 weeks I visited a lot of places. City buildings, individual homes, markets, etc. None were as nice as the apartment I stayed in. Clifford's place is top notch, the finish is fantastic. Linda decorated it, and she knows how to make a place feel like home. The bed was comfortable. The internet was reasonably fast. The living room was very comfortable; my bride and I spent a lot of time in there planning our next day. I actually loved to go to the back window and just look out over the corn field growing next door. The green of the Rift Valley and the sound of rustling corn was a lot like where I grew up in America. 
Nakuru felt very safe to me. I loved the city, the land of Nakuru County, and the people were friendly and warm. I found much of the food I like to eat in the markets downtown, as well as new foods that I had never tried before. Goat, for instance, turns out to be delicious. I had no idea. Buy some fruit from the vendors on the street. Kenyan oranges are sweet as fruit gets, the grapes are amazing, and the bananas great. And for Pete's sake, if you've never had a beef chili samosa, get one into your face at first opportunity. They are Kenya's tacos. And better than tacos. I had no idea I would ever think that way about any food. 
Clifford and Linda were friendly, knowledgeable, and willing to take a call at any hour if a problem existed. But go to the Hyrax Flora gatemen first, they know so much about how to fix things. I made sure they got huge tips by local standards, which helped a lot. Remember that if you can, it makes help very easy to find. 
I would have given this place a higher rating if there was one. And when I go back to Kenya, which I will because I'm now married to a Kenyan, the Nook@Hyrax will be where I go if my destination is Nakuru or within 50km of there. It's that good.

The cabin itself is cosy and full of character, though it can get a bit chilly at night – I’d recommend bringing an extra blanket or requesting one from the hosts. I would have appreciated a bit more variety in the pillows, as I prefer very soft ones, but this is a minor suggestion.
The friendly dogs on the property were a delightful addition, and the hosts were incredibly welcoming and helpful throughout my stay. The grounds are also fantastic for camping, and I am already planning to return with my tent for a camping trip.
Overall, it was a positive experience, and I’d highly recommend this property to anyone looking for a peaceful retreat.

We were  warmly welcomed by the whole staff team and they helped us carrying our luggage to the house. The house and the surrounding was just stunning, like living a dream, since there were so many beautiful animals  nearby the house. While enjoying breakfast, three giraffes were joining in the „garden“.  Another special moment was watching zebras grazing around the house at night. 
Josephine and her colleagues were so friendly and they prepared lovely breakfasts for us and supported us with dish washing. Food and drinks have to be bought upfront, since there is no shop on the island. 
 We booked a great boat ride where we saw hippos and many other animals. Also, we went to Hells Gate NP and climbed the Mount Longonot. It was also great! 
We stayed for four nights and we would have loved to stay forever :)

review_text:
I visited giraffe house with 6 of my friends and we spread across the main house and the owls nest, which were greatly equipped and neat. 
Judith and Brenda made our stay phenomenal. We could not thank them enough for taking care of us so generously. They cooked delicious and wholesome food, that fueled us for our explorations. Their attentiveness was outstanding and made us not have a worry in the world. 
The surroundings are of course the highlight. Expect to see zebras and impalas in the garden, monkey on the terrace (beware, they WILL steal any food you leave unattended for even a second) and beautiful birds all around you. The rangers were also always helpful with any questions, like finding the hippos and giraffes and in our case even fighting off an ostrich. Don’t miss out out on the night game drive and the hippo feeding!!
Overall the pictures don’t do this place justice, it honestly felt like garden eden, unlike anything we’ve experienced before. We will definitely be back?

In other places that I have visited, you could only stay on designated paths.  Because Sanctuary Farms have few predators, there was so much more freedom to move around.  
Rose Cottage itself was nice.  It was well maintained, functional, clean, and comfortable.  We especially loved the fire pit on the front porch.  Rose Cottage was the perfect blend between adventure, exploring, and relaxing.  I would go again if I have the opportunity.
